## Source, documentation and consumer association

The independently compared owners against audited `18ff14860ff41c084b1db5f396bb62aa9c22b1be` include formatter, zone converter/native clock, prayer model, actual `drawArc(M)` and visible render loop. All selected spans agree exactly. `qualification/currentness.json` also records current admission and prayer owners. The retained source TAP contains 126 passes with zero failures, skipped cases or TODOs, including original mutants, year/leap/Kathmandu/exact-prayer boundaries and forward/backward clock controls.

Every selected functional input was compared with its current case packet. The existing Node fixture generator was used read-only to independently regenerate the observed HTML and verify its source, fixture and observation hashes. All 46 functional case bindings match. The same binding check was applied to presentation and selected preservation acquisitions. The generated root/offline/iframe cases use their actual entries; the fixture never substitutes an expected model result for the actual consumer.

The driver and observer preserve natural document boot, native timers/performance/animation frames and actual provider ingress. The current-body hold is released through the normal JSON settlement path. The observer reads the actual render after return and does not manually invoke model, render or `qaState()` to make a result. The later video-only acquisition avoids screenshot calls and gives the encoder a bounded native one-second presentation tail; it does not advance the controlled prayer clock or pause the product scheduler.

Repository README lines 238–252 were checked against source and outcomes. The formatter rounds to the nearest second before selecting hours plus whole minutes, whole minutes, or seconds. Retained native controls include 58.4 seconds → `58s`, 59.6 seconds → `1m`, and 3599.6 seconds → `1h 0m`. Missing or unsupported precision is not documented as a zero duration or an invented next-day record. The recovery wording is explicitly the next eligible visible render, which the frozen dirty-frame control supports.

## Native functional and first-presentation findings

`functional/` contains 23 cases per engine, including the intended rejected variants. Their current values and independent UTC endpoints were checked, not merely their aggregate statuses. Final functional selection preserves the original Chromium frozen 12-hour acquisition and the matched Firefox spring-24/frozen-12 acquisitions; the public paths are already normalized to their selected cases.

Both engines measured native arc SHA256 `73758a0e4a589f735f3ecaf6dd6fed395d75b295a48454ccd2318c54fa3ead7c` for each original/wall pair in spring, first fall and ordinary controls. Geometry equality covers `.c`, `.arc`, `.cn`, `.nt`, `.left`, `.times`, `.buckle`, `.d`, `#ce` and `#ah`. I inspected all 46 original functional cards through full-resolution sheets and representative individual original arc, mutant and recovery PNGs. The actual marker representation, six rows, header and footer remain intact. This is not an assertion of whole-image equality across a dynamic sky.

For first current presentation, use `presentation/chromium/` and `presentation/firefox/`, except that Firefox `DOC-duration-seconds58` and `DOC-duration-round-to-hour` use `headed-replacement/firefox/`. The 28 original presentation acquisitions remain retained. In the accepted headed replacements, the first current frames are respectively 0031 and 0023, and already contain the correct countdown, next time, six rows, readable header and footer. The replaced headless frames are not silently promoted: seconds58 frame 0028 has a header white band; round-to-hour frame 0023 loses labels/rows/footer text and frame 0024 is later healthy.

The initial still-capture driver correctly detected receipt ordinal 2 versus before/after ordinal 3 and retained `PARTIAL_FIRST_PRESENTATION_REVIEW_REQUIRED` plus `captureMismatches`. This review does **not** turn that assertion into a PASS. Native video instead supplies the actual first presented prayer surface, while the exhaustive unchanged expected prayer fields across completed current renders rule out a wrong intervening countdown. Initial ordinal 2 and 3 prayer surfaces agree; the footer badge can arrive at ordinal 3, so whole-card byte identity and attribution to unique ordinal 2 are not proven. A few later Chromium renders move the next-time vertical coordinate by 0.5 px; no all-ordinal whole-geometry equality is claimed. These limitations do not violate the original first-presented prayer contract, which does not require inventing a unique-ordinal gate when consecutive correct prayer surfaces agree. Native first-current pictures, typography and footer were inspected directly rather than accepting a later still as the first frame.

Frozen recovery has the stronger exact association. Accepted epoch is `1772944200000` (2026-03-08 04:30Z), target is `1772960400000` (09:00Z), and elapsed time is 270 minutes. `TIMESCALE=0`, `FOLLOW_WALL_CLOCK=false` and `ADVANCING=false` agree before and after actual held tomorrow settlement. Earliest valid receipt and before/after recovered-still ordinals are identical: Chromium 24-hour = 6, Chromium 12-hour = 7, Firefox 24-hour = 6, Firefox 12-hour = 6. There is no clock step or manual render call. The sec-only mutant admits tomorrow but never paints recovered precision; the epoch-plus-24-hours mutant produces the wrong 330 minutes. A separate naturally advancing recovery control is not substituted for this frozen proof.

## Selected continuous preservation and retained failures

Use these eight qualified preservation acquisitions:

| Engine | Accepted paths |
|---|---|
| Chromium | `preservation/chromium/shared-preservation-no-preference`, `shared-preservation-reduce`, `shared-preservation-reduce-full`, and `R0007-warm-ashen-below-horizon` |
| Firefox | `headed-replacement/firefox/shared-preservation-no-preference`, `shared-preservation-reduce`, `shared-preservation-reduce-full`, and `R0007-warm-ashen-below-horizon` |

The installed engines are Chromium 148.0.7778.96 and Firefox 150.0.2 on Windows AMD64. Viewport is 370×570, DPR 1, card 325×530. Current acquisitions use Playwright 1.60.0; the retained successful Chromium frozen 12-hour case uses 1.57.0 with the same installed Chromium engine. Each browser identity records the executable binary hash. Headed Firefox changes only `headless=false`; the installed engine, SDK, inputs, fixture, viewport and native recorder are unchanged. This establishes a usable bounded acquisition route, not a causal finding about why the headless originals lost regions.

The headless Firefox preservation originals remain failed continuous evidence. Examples independently inspected include default frame 0623 at 24.88 seconds with its Fajr row removed by a white band, full-override frame 0463 at 18.48 seconds with a row band, reduced-motion frame 0057 blank, and warm-ashen frame 0127 with a broad middle band. Direct independent decoding of the original default WebM at 24.88 seconds reproduced retained frame 0623 bytes (SHA256 `22b0ab40042933e56b525f8aa096fc47e8b5da55b647b922fbf622fc0e02302a`). A later healthy frame does not repair these watches. No renderer/encoder/compositor cause is asserted.

The accepted Firefox default headed control contains 841 native frames; headed reduced contains 836; headed full override contains 845; headed warm ashen contains 450. I inspected original keyframes, full-card 15-second/end pixels, and unscaled one-second native temporal sequences. Exhaustive decoded-frame scans for the observed interior white-band defect supplied additional defect locations, never a visual PASS oracle. No late counterpart was found in the headed sequences; early blank loading frames remain disclosed. I do not claim to have manually read every individual decoded frame or to certify all possible continuous visual defects. The retained continuous native clips and inspected temporal pixels establish the required supported motion over the actual approximately 30-second watch, with a readable stable card in the accepted states.

Default and forced-full sequences visibly change cloud structure/position; reduced preference suppresses the motion after initial adoption. Their actual preference receipts are respectively false/false/false, true/false/true and true/true/false for OS-reduced / force-full / effective-reduced. These controls use native Date and no `simTime` or `timeScale`; the controlled broken-cloud weather and Honolulu location are explicit. Only two prayer requests occur over roughly 35–37 completed renders in these watches, providing no evidence of a per-frame request storm. No `qaState().clouds.hash` is used as motion proof.

Warm current Moon evidence is deliberately separate from first-prayer proof. Chromium is current at the selected 15/30-second checkpoints. Firefox is not current at 15 seconds and receives no Moon acceptance credit there; the 30-second admitted terrain preview is current. Both warm-ashen controls are current and show the faint opaque body mostly in frame with no stars visible through the disc. The ashen inputs explicitly force phase 0.01 and altitude −20 degrees at fixed `1772951400000`; native up is zero. Consumed physical moonlight/beam/cloud-light/wash/glow/halo/corona/paraselenae contributions are all zero. Pixels and these receipts support a calendar disc without fabricated moonlight.

The separate post-capture diagnostic uses the existing Moon state interface. Its getter can adopt a pending preview; the acquisition therefore compares material href and visible card class before/after. All selected receipts show exactly unchanged visible surface. This check does not claim the getter is intrinsically side-effect-free. The current Moon is a terrain preview with the retained 0.0416 px phase bound, not final angular-refinement or startup-science acceptance.

## Artifact verification, commands and inspected material

At artifact head `69b4b19bebd31e940095b089e5a01a7ed60a3b0a`, the independent public-packet verifier checked all 883 manifest entries for length, compressed SHA256 and decompressed SHA256, parsed JSON including gzip payloads, and recursively inspected string values for private absolute filesystem locators: zero mismatches and zero private locators. All 88 public raw traces, after decompression, exactly match the retained original acquisition bytes. The packet has 46 functional, 28 presentation, eight original preservation and six headed-replacement acquisitions; these are acquisition counts, not 88 distinct passing cases.

The review found a publication-only defect in an earlier, unpublished projection: 46 nested browser executable paths survived JSON escaping in `qualification/independent-checks.json.gz`. The corrected artifact projects these to basename plus binary hash and records projection/original receipt identity; the private originals are unchanged. The artifact README now also identifies the inherited SDK 1.57.0 exception. Both fixes were independently read back. This is a repaired packaging defect, not a new runtime change.

Read-only command evidence includes `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}'`, `git status --porcelain`, canonical `git show` of the immutable specification and audited source, and `git diff --name-only 87c3a19ff275197e1a49bebd7abc30ad2849137e HEAD -- . ':!docs/rlgwo-execution/20261014/R0007'` (empty). Reviewer helpers were invoked with Python `-I -B`. Their private reviewer-workspace filenames are `independent_checks.py`, `native_tail_checks.py` (original and headed lanes), `white_band_locator.py`, and `public_packet_checks.py`; these helper names are not public artifact paths. The primary case inputs, native evidence and source-currentness results they check are bound in the public packet. The fixture comparison invokes the existing Node fixture generator with the actual entry and saved case input. Native frame extraction used the installed FFmpeg. The first attempted frame-select helper option was unsupported by that minimal build; the subsequent native timestamp decode succeeded. No unsupported helper command is counted as evidence.

Material inspected includes the canonical specification and issue receipts; repository `README.md`, `src/native/index.html`, root and offline generated entries, fixture/case packets and browser driver/runtime; `qualification/currentness.json`, runtime inventory, source TAP and projected independent receipt; all functional original cards and native traces; original/mutant arc PNGs; exact recovered PNGs and presentation receipts; video-only transition strips and individual first frames; original failed headless preservation frames; selected headed and Chromium temporal sequences, full-card warm/15-second/end frames and preservation receipts; `cases.json`, `manifest.json`, packet README and closure-certificate state. `qualification/public-consumer-before/readback.json` and all four root/V1 original PNGs were also inspected. ## Limits and remaining action

Unavailable date text can retain the existing footer ellipsis; the current date disclosure/dialog contract remains in source. This is not new layout drift from R0007. The review does not award a new whole-scene startup PASS, qualify unrelated weather recording, reopen accepted astronomical work, certify final Moon science, or close another RLGWO. Earlier acquisition failures and original PARTIAL statuses remain evidence, with accepted replacements selected explicitly.

The pre-delivery public consumer receipt proves the existing deployed runtime identity, not delivery of the changed README or this packet. At review time the closure certificate correctly reserves external delivery fields. The primary may incorporate this report and update qualification metadata. Any resulting artifact-only head requires the promised narrow source/tree/manifest readback; this review is not an authorization to merge that future head. Final owner-approved delivery must complete 7.16.b before a completed issue closure can be claimed.
